So, seven thirty, not eight. Is that right? And breakfast?
That is right. Breakfast is from seven, so you have half an hour.
Perfect. And in the afternoon? Is there anything?
Nothing until five thirty. And dinner is at eight, in the evening. Please be early — the restaurant is small.

Morning now. On Friday at ten. It changed this afternoon.

Hi, it's Paul, your driver. I am calling about tomorrow, because there are two changes and I do not want you to wait in the street. First, I come at seven thirty in the morning, not at eight. I know we said eight, but the traffic on Thursday is very bad after eight, so we need the extra half hour. Second, in the afternoon I cannot come at five, because I have another car at that time. My colleague comes instead, and his name is Tomas. Same car, different driver. Everything else is the same: dinner at eight, and I take you back to the hotel after that. If seven thirty is too early, call me tonight, not tomorrow morning. Thank you, and good night.

People ask me how I do it, so here is my day, and it is not complicated. I get up at five thirty, every day, and I do not use an alarm any more. From six to seven I walk, always, and that is the only hour of the day that is only mine. I have breakfast at seven with my children, and after that the day belongs to other people. I start work at eight thirty and I stop at six, and I do not answer the phone after eight in the evening. On Saturday I work in the morning, but never in the afternoon. On Sunday I do nothing, and that is not laziness, it is the reason the other six days work. I go to bed at ten. That is it. No secret.
Good morning. What time is the car tomorrow? At seven thirty, not at eight? And the meeting is at nine, is that right? I finish at eleven. See you in the morning.
